articles.title: Prediction markets win big on election night
articles.author: Jake Angelo
articles.summary: Prediction markets emerged as big winners of the midterms. Kalshi and Polymarket correctly called the Democratic sweep of Congress by wider margins than most polling models, as well as key battleground races, though they missed surprises like Texas Gov. Greg Abbott’s loss and Democratic Senate victories in Iowa and South Carolina. Trading volume on down-ballot elections grew nearly fivefold from the 2024 cycle to this year’s midterms to $1.8 billion, according to a Semafor analysis of the sites’ public data feeds. Sports and crypto bets still dwarf election contracts across both platforms, and the 2026 midterms attracted less trading interest than the presidential race. Prediction markets have been racing to win over the sports-betting and gambling industries’ customers, executing aggressive ad campaigns to expand their influence. Kalshi has struck business partnerships with media outlets including CNN and Dow Jones, and its ad campaign on Meta rivals super PAC spending ; Kalshi and Polymarket have also aired a slew of star-studded ads. But it’s one thing to bring in revenue, it’s another to do what the prediction markets say they do well: predict. — Jake Angelo

articles.title: Impeach Pete Hegseth for the Disastrous Iran War
articles.author: Gene Healy
articles.summary: Democrats took the House of Representatives and Senate Tuesday night in large part thanks to voter backlash against President Donald Trump's disastrous war of choice against Iran. When the House returns for the lame-duck session, one of the first items of business—whether outgoing Speaker Mike Johnson (R–La.) likes it or not—will be revisiting the articles of impeachment lodged against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth for "high crimes and misdemeanors" related to that war. Johnson rushed the House to early recess in mid-September to avoid a vote on Hegseth's impeachment. But the articles, drawn up by outgoing Rep. Thomas Massie (R–Ky.), are coming back when the House returns. The GOP gadfly recently announced he intends to force a vote on " week one ." Massie's effort has a real shot even under lame duck math , before the new Democratic majority comes in. Passing it will require only a handful of GOP votes. In September, seven Republicans split from their party to vote for withdrawal from Iran. After Tuesday's electoral shellacking, GOP members should be looking for clear opportunities to distance themselves from Trump's disastrous and unnecessary war. Here's their chance to do that—
